inventory.title: Sidequest — Three Days of Games in Rotterdam
inventory.description: An independent games festival in Rotterdam: talks, a 64-player tournament, and a late-night arcade. 14–16 March, three venues, no press passes.
inventory.tagline: Three days of *games you haven't heard of yet*
inventory.lede: Fifty-one playable builds, eleven talks, one 64-player tournament, and an arcade that stays open until the trams stop. Three venues along the Maas, one wristband, no press passes.

items.title: Fifty-one builds, *most of them unfinished*
items.note: Every machine on the floor is attended by someone who made it. They will hand you the controller and watch your face. Ask them anything.

features.title: Talks, a tournament, *and a floor that never closes early*
features.note: Panels run 11:00–17:00 in the old grain silo. From 21:00 the arcade takes over two rooms on Schiekade and runs until 02:00.

about.title: Four people, *one very long spreadsheet*
about.note: Sidequest started in 2021 as a zine about Dutch game jams. The festival is what happened when we ran out of pages.

contact.title: Questions, *access needs, or a build to submit*
contact.note: We answer everything within two working days. For lost-property during the festival, use the phone number — we are not at the desk.

features.name: Talks in the silo
features.detail: Eleven talks across two days, 25 minutes each, no slides longer than nine words. All recorded and posted free within a week.

features.name: The 64-player tournament
features.detail: One game, single elimination, Saturday from 13:00. Bring your own stick or use ours. Sign-up closes when the bracket fills, usually by Friday evening.

features.name: Late arcade
features.detail: Two rooms on Schiekade, 21:00–02:00 Friday and Saturday. Thirty-one cabinets and a wall of CRTs, all on free play with your wristband.

features.name: Quiet room
features.detail: A dimmed room on the second floor with beanbags, water, and no sound above 45 decibels. Open whenever the building is. No booking, no queue.

features.name: Build clinic
features.detail: Sunday 10:00–13:00: bring a project, sit with two working developers for 40 minutes, leave with a list. Free, twelve slots, sign up at the door.

aboutBody: Sidequest began as a photocopied zine about Dutch game jams — 60 copies, stapled at a kitchen table in Kralingen. We kept a running list of every unfinished build we liked, and by 2023 the list was longer than the zine. The festival is that list, with chairs.

We are four people with day jobs. We do not take sponsorship from publishers, we do not run a business track, and we do not have a press lounge. What we have is three venues, a borrowed PA, and a rule that anyone showing work gets a free wristband and a meal. Everything else is on the page above.
inventory.footerNote: Sidequest is run by four people and a spreadsheet. Wristbands are non-refundable but freely transferable.

pullQuote.text: Nobody here is going to ask you what your studio's funding model is. They are going to ask what happens when you press the second button.
pullQuote.attribution: Ines Bakhuizen, programmer, at the 2024 build clinic

process.name: Pick a day
process.detail: Friday is talks and the first arcade night. Saturday is the tournament. Sunday is quiet, with the build clinic and the last playable hours.

process.name: Buy a wristband
process.detail: One wristband covers all three venues and both arcade nights. Single-day tickets exist; they do not include the tournament.

process.name: Show up
process.detail: Doors open 10:30. Bring ID if you want to drink. Bring a controller if you are fussy about controllers.

process.name: Stay late
process.detail: The arcade runs to 02:00. Night buses from Schiekade every 20 minutes; the last one is at 02:40.
